headline: Highest risk is cascading error: OpenMetadata can ingest and act on upstream outputs via MCP/APIs, while godot_rl_agents has no documented output-verification or safety controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no shared channel or I/O surface, so direct injection into it is not documented. OpenMetadata can expose MCP/APIs/webhooks, which could bridge content into other systems if manually wired. Because the pairwise path is undocumented and depends on external wiring, severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator wires OpenMetadata outputs into godot_rl_agents inputs via files, MCP, or copy-paste, then prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF no shared channel is configured, then this risk remains absent.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any automatic file or message handoff between them.
Review any MCP bridge before enabling it.
Use manual copy-paste only for sanitized summaries.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: godot_rl_agents has network egress set to none and no data classes touched, so it is not a leakage source in the profile. OpenMetadata touches governance and lineage metadata and can call APIs/webhooks, but no shared workspace or sensitive data class is documented. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited and not default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or dataset, then metadata may flow from OpenMetadata into the other agent's context.
IF OpenMetadata is configured to send webhook payloads containing sensitive fields, then leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place both agents on the same shared folder.
Restrict OpenMetadata webhooks to non-sensitive metadata.
Verify outbound API destinations in OpenMetadata.
Keep godot_rl_agents offline from any shared storage.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction on OpenMetadata exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or shared-resource permissions, while OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and interacts through APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. Without a documented shared mutable target, direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, so the lower-but-nonzero conflict risk is low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API, database, or webhook target, then conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a mutable directory between them, then file-level contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Serialize any writes through one orchestrator.
Check OpenMetadata target credentials before enabling writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata is built for data collaboration/governance and can consume events, APIs, and MCP inputs, so it may treat upstream content as authoritative if not verified. godot_rl_agents has no documented verification or downstream-action controls, making a bad upstream output more likely to propagate. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are fed into OpenMetadata as facts or lineage updates without validation, then errors can cascade.
IF OpenMetadata is configured to auto-ingest events from the other agent, then downstream propagation is possible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ingestion.
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs.
Limit OpenMetadata to read-only consumption for this pair.
Log and diff imported records before publishing.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data-class mismatch is documented for either agent. godot_rl_agents touches no data classes and has no egress; OpenMetadata's metadata surfaces are documented but not tied to a conflicting compliance regime. With no compliance mismatch evidence, the pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into OpenMetadata and routed to a noncompliant deployment, then compliance risk may arise.
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is later documented, reassess this verdict.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document retention settings for OpenMetadata.
Confirm deployment region before onboarding sensitive data.
Review access logs weekly.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated fields.
